title: I Let the Community Ice-Bath Wristband Survive Three Evenings After They Waived the Desk

parts.text: I checked in at 7:04 p.m. and host Kai had already waived the desk for friends. The board said: WRISTBANDS NIGHTLY. DESK LOGS EVERY DIP. I was thirty-one, plunge steward, holding a clipboard that listed our tub. Kai shrugged. "Hosts are the water." I photographed the board, the waived line, and an unmarked wrist on tub two. Then I asked for the wristband log. At 7:12 the desk pinged a dip with no band.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Tub two just logged a dip with no wristband.

social.video_title: They waived the ice-bath desk for friends — Part 1/3
social.description: Nightly bands, a waived desk, an unmarked wrist on tub two. Would you have asked for the wristband log?

parts.text: Tuesday the unmarked wrist was back. I printed Monday's still and taped it to the board. Kai called it hospitality. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. The board now has the still. At 7:18 the desk asked why tub two skipped the band two nights running. Kai said optics. Optics is a word hosts use when a desk exists.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The unmarked wrist is back; the board now has the still.

social.video_title: Tub two skipped the band two nights — Part 2/3
social.description: Hospitality, a still on the board, a skipped band. Was a friend ever the desk?

parts.text: Thursday the board added a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE WATER. Kai ran his own band and told the next host atmosphere was always about optics. I keep our bands in a labeled tin. The desk logs every dip. Kai brown-bags his waivers. The tub finally looks like a booking, not a favor. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the water — Part 3/3
social.description: Second line on the board, labeled tin, desk logs every dip. Was hospitality ever an unmarked wrist?
